svg.text: 21 × 16 grid · cols 1–21, rows A–P · component side from above · solder on the underside · generated by make_wiring_map.py
v6 FIX: the two Pico rows were SWAPPED in v5. USB at col 1 ⇒ row B (upper) = pins 40…21 POWER, row I (lower) = pins 1…20 GPIO
3V3_OUT is B5, not I5 · SDA/SCL are I6/I7 · GPS UART moved to GP16/GP17 = B20/B19 · BAT+ pad moved to A2
USB at col 1 ⇒ row B = pins 40…21 (POWER) row I = pins 1…20 (GPIO)
elevated ~8.5 mm on sockets · rows C–H beneath are free
v6 rework is COMPLETE -- rails, feeds and both Pico rows verified
clean by socket_selftest.py on 2026-08-03. Nothing left to undo.
v7 CHANGE: both sensor breakouts are seated with pin 1 at the HIGH
column end, so the silkscreen order runs right-to-left. Every
sensor-side jumper below moved. VERIFY against the real boards
before soldering: MPU VCC must be the pin nearest column 9, and
BMP VIN the pin nearest column 19.
I3 → K3 GND feed I3(p3) → rail
J13 → L13 TIE CS→3V3 = I²C mode
L6 → N6 → N14 → L14 SDA chain → BMP SDI
L7 → O7 → O16 → L16 SCL chain → BMP SCK
B20 → A16 GP16 TX → GPS RX
B19 → A15 GPS TX → GP17 RX
J13 → A13 GPS VCC (long run under the Pico)
K14 → A14 GPS GND (long run under the Pico)
1. cut board to 21 × 16 · sharpie the A1 corner on BOTH faces [done]
2. socket strips B + I (Pico), L (MPU 2–9, BMP 12–19), A (GPS 13–16) [done]
3. rails: row J cols 2–19, row K cols 1–19, bare solid wire [done]
4. rail feeds B5→J5 (3V3) and I3→K3 (GND) [done, verified]
5. sensor power taps J9→L9, K8→L8, J19→L19, K17→L17
6. ⚠ THE TWO TIES K15→L15 (SDO→GND, addr 0x76) and J13→L13 (CS→3V3, I²C mode)
7. I²C feeds I6→L6 (SDA), I7→L7 (SCL), then the two chains via rows N and O
8. GPS: UART B20→A16, B19→A15 · power J13→A13, K14→A14
9. battery pads A2 / K1 and their leads LAST — meter the pack polarity first
• after step 4 — board must still enumerate over USB. The J rail is fed from the
Pico's own 3V3 supply, so a J–K short stops it booting entirely.
• after step 5 — beep J→L9 and J→L19; beep K→L8 and K→L17. Then J against K.
• after step 6 — L15 beeps to K (GND) · L13 beeps to J (3V3) · they must NOT beep together.
• after step 7 — L6 beeps to L14 (SDA) · L7 beeps to L16 (SCL) · SDA NOT to SCL.
• any time — run socket_selftest.py — the Pico finds its own socket bridges.
• first power-up — i2c.scan() → [0x68, 0x76]. 0x77 = SDO tie failed. empty = CS tie.
• B1–B6 are the POWER pins: VBUS B1 · VSYS B2 · GND B3 · 3V3_EN B4 · 3V3_OUT B5 · ADC_VREF B6
• a bridge at B2–B3 shorts 5 V to ground — the one destructive fault on this board
• ⚠ B4 is 3V3_EN, NOT a supply. It is the regulator's ENABLE, held high by a weak (~100k)
pull-up. Feeding the rail from B4 works with nothing attached, then collapses the
instant any load appears — the load drags EN low and switches the regulator OFF.
Symptom: enumerates bare, dies the moment a sensor is plugged in. (Hit 2026-08-03.)
The supply is B5 = 3V3_OUT. Count from the USB end: B1 B2 B3 B4 B5.
• I1/I2 = GP0/GP1, now UNUSED (UART moved to GP16/GP17). Keep I2 clear of the I3 ground joint.
• ○ A1/A20/O1/O20 = M2 screw holes → sled bosses (48.26 × 35.56 mm) — solder low nearby
• dashed jumpers are long runs beneath the elevated Pico · everything crossing a bare rail is insulated
• sensor bodies sit ~8.5 mm up on their sockets and overhang the bare J/K rails —
clearance is fine, but keep the rail wire flat and its solder blobs low
• free: rows C–H under the Pico · cols 20–21 on most rows · rows M and P
